clue.text: Where you rave till you drop?

definitions.text: Where you rave till you drop?

parts.words: Where you rave till you drop?
parts.note: reads as an all-night dance do, but a soldiers' work detail on menial duty is named after weariness

explanation.surface: A question about the sort of all-night party where dancers keep going until they collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: The military sense is a squad detailed for menial chores; the clue pretends it is a party that leaves you exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: In army slang a fatigue is a menial chore and a party is a detail of soldiers, so the phrase names a work squad.

clue.text: Runabout in Spaghetti Junction?

parts.note: a runabout looks like a small car, but here it is a road that runs above another at a tangled motorway interchange

explanation.surface: A small car driving round a notoriously tangled motorway interchange.
explanation.walkthrough: Spaghetti Junction is the nickname of a huge, tangled motorway interchange in Birmingham, England, full of elevated roads.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevated road crossing above another is a typical feature of a complex motorway interchange.

clue.text: However right this divine type's passe

parts.note: the clipped spelling tho' is an old-fashioned way of writing 'though', meaning however

explanation.surface: A grumble that this sort of godlike figure is out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passe' points to the dated clipped spelling of 'though'. The answer is the Norse god of thunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norse god of thunder is a deity, a figure of the divine kind.

clue.text: Nell meeting editor's daughter in Welsh county

parts.note: Nell Gwyn was the actress and mistress of Charles II
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A woman named Nell meets an editor's daughter somewhere in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-western Welsh region around Snowdonia is a county of Wales.

clue.text: The changes imposed on one state in accordance with moral standards

indicators.note: the word 'The' changes, so its three letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A government imposes changes on a state to make it behave more morally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns THE into ETH; 'imposed on' simply puts that before I and CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in line with principles of right conduct is what being principled or moral means.

clue.text: Runner in a rage

parts.note: ire is anger, a synonym of rage

explanation.surface: Someone running in a furious temper.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'runner' in crosswords is often a river; this one flows through Leeds in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river runs, so crosswords call one a runner; this is a Yorkshire river.

clue.text: Woman drinks vermouth as a Shakespearean character

indicators.note: one piece drinks another, taking it inside itself

parts.note: Tania is a woman's name
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A woman drinking vermouth while dressed as a figure from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinks' puts IT inside TANIA, after its first letter. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy queen in A Midsummer Night's Dream is one of Shakespeare's characters.

clue.text: Acumen Alma dug up with distinction

indicators.note: 'dug up' suggests the letters are turned over and churned, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Acumen shown by a graduate of her alma mater is unearthed with honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges ACUMEN, ALMA and DUG into the Latin graduation phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is an honour on a university degree, meaning 'with great praise'.

clue.text: Description of empty cargo ships possibly indicating unbridled competition?

definitions.text: Description of empty cargo ships possibly
definitions.meaning: ships carrying nothing have nothing in their storage spaces below deck
a contest with no rules or restrictions at all

explanation.surface: Empty freighters taken as a sign of a cut-throat market.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a ship's cargo spaces are its holds, so empty ones have none; idiomatically the phrase, from wrestling, means without restrictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally it says no cargo spaces are filled; as an idiom from wrestling it means a contest with no restrictions.

clue.text: No special person in a New York organisation

parts.note: a body is an organised group, an organisation

explanation.surface: An ordinary person working for a New York organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone is just one of the crowd means they are an ordinary person, nobody in particular.

clue.text: Nelson's cry of exultation, 28 getting correspondence?

parts.note: ho is an exclamation of triumph or exultation
a ratio is a correspondence, a proportional relation between quantities

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson shouts in triumph on receiving his letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The '28' in the feed is a stray from the newspaper page and plays no part. 'Correspondence' means a proportional relation, not letters; the definition is the admiral's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral famous for Trafalgar had this as his first name.

clue.text: Scoundrel broadcast from part of church

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard spoken, so a word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a knave is a rogue or scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain's voice is broadcast from inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of the word for scoundrel is silent, so it sounds like the central body of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The main body of a church, where the congregation sits, is a part of the building.

clue.text: What to do to one in college?

definitions.text: What to do to one in college?

parts.words: What to do to one in college?
parts.note: the person in college is a student, and what a lecturer does to students is instruct them

explanation.surface: A question about what to do to someone at college.
explanation.definitionFit: Instructing pupils is the job done to students at a college.

clue.text: As before, to print part of account only

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the letters sit inside the run 'account only'

explanation.surface: Accounting instructions to print only part of an account, as previously done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks the definition as an old-fashioned word for 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical, archaic preposition means 'to', so it is a dated form of the word.

clue.text: Dome exploited by Liberal for example

indicators.note: something exploited is worked over and reused, so the letters of Dome are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician exploiting a dome building, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern or exemplar to copy is a standard instance, an example of the kind.

clue.text: Reportedly having no interest in directors

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said aloud, so a word sounds like another

parts.note: someone bored has no interest in what is going on

explanation.surface: Rumour has it the company's directors are uninterested.
explanation.definitionFit: The directors of a company sit together as its governing body.

clue.text: Golf boy holding ball for 4 or 5?

parts.note: a Volkswagen Golf is a car

indicators.note: the boy is holding the ball, so it goes inside

parts.note: lad is a word for a boy
O is ball-shaped, so it stands for a ball

explanation.surface: A boy holding a golf ball for the fourth or fifth hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf' is the Volkswagen model, not the game; '4 or 5' is the number of people who fit in a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Four or five people is the number a typical motor vehicle can hold.

clue.text: One's cooking eaten by fat man

indicators.note: one piece is eaten by another, so it goes inside it

parts.note: lard is cooking fat

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of 'One' are mixed up

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone's cooking is wolfed down by a fat man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges ONE into EON; 'eaten by' puts that inside LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common boy's name, so it defines a man.

clue.text: Estate could fail given this word by international 3

parts.note: mot is French for word, also used in English as in bon mot
a Test is an international match in cricket or rugby

explanation.surface: A property estate might fail, judged by a word from an international figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '3' is from the newspaper page and plays no part. 'Estate' is an estate car; the British annual roadworthiness check can fail it. A Test is an international cricket or rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's yearly roadworthiness inspection of vehicles can fail an estate car.

clue.text: Nervous time with wife wanting to scratch

parts.note: itchy skin makes you want to scratch

explanation.surface: A nervous moment when a wife longs to scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpy and jittery describes a person who is anxious.

clue.text: Sailor gets a score in darts reduced in array of figures

indicators.note: the sailor gets the other pieces put inside him
the sailor gets the other pieces put inside him

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: reduced means a letter is cut from the end

parts.note: a bull is the bullseye, a score in darts

explanation.surface: A sailor scores a bullseye in a darts match, then has his tally cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts BULL to BUL; 'gets ... in' puts A and BUL inside TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Data set out in rows and columns, like a table of numbers, is arranged in that form.

clue.text: Upset over a description of champagne by traveller 4

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: brut describes a very dry champagne
a rep is a travelling salesman

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman upset over the description given of some champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '4' is from the newspaper page and plays no part. 'over' turns BRUT and REP together, giving PER then TURB.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb or unsettle someone is to make them anxious, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Have old law enforcers put on ship

parts.note: a posse is a body of men summoned by a sheriff in the old West
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Old-time sheriff's men are placed aboard a steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places the ship after the posse in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something or hold it as property is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Flying up into a perfectly described state?

indicators.note: flying means the letters scatter about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Soaring up into an ideal land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' rearranges UP, INTO and A; the definition refers to Thomas More's ideal island.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's ideal island described a perfect society, and the adjective means relating to such an idealised state.

clue.text: Like a type without daughter

indicators.note: without means the letter is removed

parts.note: kind means sort or type

explanation.surface: Something resembling a sort of person who has no daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being related or similar to something means resembling it.

clue.text: Lower a floor level

parts.note: the base is the bottom level, the floor

explanation.surface: Bring a floor down to a lower level.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble or degrade someone is to bring them down in rank, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Lively type who gets the green light?

definitions.meaning: an energetic, enthusiastic person always ready for fun
a green traffic signal tells a driver to move on

explanation.surface: An energetic person who is given permission to proceed.
explanation.definitionFit: An energetic person is called this in British slang, and literally it is anyone who proceeds when the lights turn green.

clue.text: Victim of confusion losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: babel is a confused noise, after the Tower of Babel

explanation.surface: Someone harmed in the chaos loses their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the first letter of BABEL. The victim is the brother killed by Cain in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Cain's brother in Genesis was the first murder victim.

clue.text: Singular garment for priestly tribe?

indicators.note: singular means the plural S is dropped to leave one

parts.note: Levis are a brand of denim jeans

explanation.surface: A single item of clothing worn by a tribe of priests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' drops the plural S of the jeans brand; the tribe is the Israelite tribe from which priests came.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelite tribe descended from Jacob's son served as the priestly tribe.

clue.text: After December 1st you'll have to live with liberal measure of sound

parts.note: 1st becomes I, the Roman numeral for one
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: After the first of December you will have to put up with a generous amount of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit used to measure loudness is a measure of sound.

clue.text: Before time for change one was a solitary monk

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: for change means the letters of 'time' are changed around

explanation.surface: Long ago, a recluse took time out to change his life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' rearranges TIME into MITE after ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit, especially a religious recluse, lives apart as a solitary monk.

clue.text: Seriously ban bad language

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A serious call to ban foul language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges SERIOUSLY and BAN; 'language' looks like part of 'bad language' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Slavic tongue of Belarus is a language.
